opportunities.title: Influence benchmarks
opportunities.objective: Build a reproducible auction and multi-agent laboratory with seeded news, counterfactual scenarios, observable behavior and resource accounting.

checks: Verify the exact topic, Phase I eligibility and current funding terms.
Confirm applicant and data/IP rights before any submission.

requirements.statement: Deterministic orders record time, asset, quantity and price; auction clearing respects balances, quantities, valuations and utility.
Demonstrate at least ten LLM-based stock-agent identities with actual provider/model/version and prompt receipts; they need not use ten providers.
Measure allocative efficiency against a disclosed optimum on repeated seeded valuation and news scenarios.
Evaluate collaboration, deception, anchoring, herding and risk-preference classifiers on independently labeled controls.
Replay orders, news, interactions and temporal/causal graph provenance from exact inputs; counterfactual labels alone do not establish causality.
Measure end-to-end latency and resource use including provider calls, retries and failures.

candidates.approach: Standard auction engine with independently configured LLM stock agents.
Graph-mediated interactions with otherwise identical auctions and news.
Deterministic event-sourced market with replayed prompts and orders.
Adapt existing task-market abstractions only after source inspection.
Reproduce an available marketplace reference under documented licensing.

architecture: Seeded asset/value model -> validated order book -> deterministic auction clearing -> utility and allocative-efficiency report.
Configured model adapters -> ten or more isolated stock-agent identities -> bounded interactions and news consumption.
Event receipts -> temporal/causal hypotheses -> labeled behavior evaluation -> claim/evidence projection.

risks.mitigation: Use randomized interventions, null controls and an independent domain review.

risks.risk: Different model costs or seeds bias a candidate bakeoff.
risks.mitigation: Match models, budgets and experiments; report failures and unmatched cases.

submission_format.notes: Owner reports a ten-page white paper, five slides and a $300,000 Phase I. Verify the current solicitation before relying on these limits.

milestones.objective: Verify official scope, rights, prerequisites and experiment targets.

evidence_missing: Official topic source and eligibility decision.

opportunities.title: NAVAIR acquisition analysis
opportunities.objective: Rank related acquisition records with deterministic top-N behavior, source explanations and a reproducible evaluation package.

checks: Locate the exact solicitation and current applicant requirements.
Resolve corpus licensing, government-furnished information and public-release rights.

requirements.statement: Extract bounded document text and metadata; report malformed, duplicate, excluded and unsupported inputs.
Return stable top-N rankings and tie-breaking with document/model provenance and reproducible query settings.
Evaluate held-out retrieval quality using independently labeled queries and leakage controls.
Measure complete parsing/indexing/query latency under a disclosed workload.
Measure peak memory for the same corpus, model and hardware configuration.
Build and execute a reproducible container or reviewed portable package with an SBOM and result receipts.

candidates.approach: Lexical BM25 baseline.
Embedding-only retrieval with a pinned model.
Calibrated lexical/vector retrieval.
Relationship graph retrieval with traceable edges.
Cluster-aware retrieval with held-out tuning.
Rerank the same candidate set and count added compute.

architecture: Authorized corpus -> parser/metadata -> lexical/vector index -> relationship graph/clustering.
Query -> deterministic candidate retrieval -> optional reranker -> ranked explanations and provenance.
Disclosed corpus/query split -> reproducibility/quality/runtime/memory receipts -> validation package.

risks.risk: Restricted acquisition text is accidentally treated as public.
risks.mitigation: Use an explicitly rights-cleared public corpus and retain exclusion receipts.

risks.risk: High retrieval scores reflect benchmark leakage.
risks.mitigation: Keep held-out relevance labels and an independent verifier.

submission_format.notes: The owner describes a containerized analysis package and validation report; official submission format and deadline are unknown.

opportunities.title: Brain-inspired low-SWaP
opportunities.objective: Compare a fixed monolithic baseline with a heterogeneous neural runtime and dynamic compute gate using controlled tasks and ablations.

checks: Verify the exact topic and whether the proposed experiment fits its Phase I scope.
Confirm scientific reviewers, public datasets and any hardware restrictions.

requirements.statement: Run a common task/dataset interface for baseline and heterogeneous candidates with repeatable seeds and configuration receipts.
Measure task accuracy, switching, novelty response and failure modes against a held-out baseline.
Measure complete latency including perception, temporal state, memory and compute-gate overhead.
Measure physical energy on the actual device with power instrumentation, sampling method and idle/preprocessing policy.
Run ablations that isolate compute gating, temporal, spiking and memory contributions from orchestration overhead.
Measure peak device memory and active parameters on a declared runtime.

candidates.approach: Fixed monolithic model baseline.
Perception plus temporal/SSM/RNN, small transformer, spiking subsystem and graph/vector memory.
The same heterogeneous components with a measured dynamic compute gate.
Remove one component or gate at a time under identical controls.

architecture: Frozen tasks -> baseline or heterogeneous perception/temporal/transformer/spiking modules -> common outputs.
Graph/vector memory and dynamic compute gating -> observable decisions and resource receipts.
Held-out quality/task-switching runs + ablations + physical instrument receipts -> scientific review.

risks.risk: Biological terminology substitutes for a research contribution.
risks.mitigation: Require ablations, a falsifiable hypothesis and independent scientific review.

risks.risk: Estimated power is presented as physical feasibility.
risks.mitigation: Require physical evidence kind and raw measurement method for hardware claims.

submission_format.notes: The owner reports that simulations and small Phase I prototypes are permitted. Official requirements and submission limits remain unverified.

evidence_missing: Official topic and domain-review assessment of novelty.

controls: Keep tasks, preprocessing, dataset splits and seeds identical across candidates.
Record measured watts separately from estimated energy; estimates cannot satisfy physical evidence.
State device, idle draw, sampling frequency, warm-up and system boundary for every power result.

opportunities.title: Semantic ISR
opportunities.objective: Compare semantic video packets and receiver reconstruction with standard codecs on public video, preserving mission relevance and uncertainty.

checks: Verify the exact topic and Direct-to-Phase-II feasibility/eligibility requirements.
Separate public prototype data from controlled information and required physical feasibility evidence.

requirements.statement: Produce H.264/H.265/AV1 baselines with matched video, rate, quality and runtime configuration.
Validate versioned semantic packets, temporal scene memory, ROI selection, bounded receiver reconstruction and packet-loss recovery.
Measure transmitted bytes including metadata, retransmission and temporal refresh under the same task and video conditions.
Evaluate receiver task utility and confidence/uncertainty calibration using held-out labels.
Measure actual edge-device end-to-end latency including capture, processing, transport and reconstruction.
Measure device power or energy with actual instrumentation; Jetson build artifacts alone are insufficient.

candidates.approach: Pinned H.264 encoder/decoder baseline.
Pinned H.265 encoder/decoder baseline.
Pinned AV1 encoder/decoder baseline.
ROI-aware encoding with transmitted metadata accounted.
Temporal graph and mission-relevance packets with traceable uncertainty.

architecture: Rights-cleared EO video -> codec baseline or temporal scene memory -> mission-relevant ROI/behavior selection.
Semantic packet + confidence -> bounded low-bandwidth channel -> receiver reconstruction.
Matched public video and labels -> bandwidth/utility/calibration receipts -> physical edge-device campaign.

risks.mitigation: Measure receiver task utility, uncertainty and failure cases alongside bandwidth.

risks.risk: Simulated deployment is confused with DP2 feasibility.
risks.mitigation: Hold physical requirements open until actual device receipts and review exist.

submission_format.notes: The owner reports DP2 qualification uncertainty and empirical device evidence requirements. No eligibility, funding or format is confirmed.
